chapter-09.md (found after normalization): '200/400GbE transcodes 64b/66b to 256b/257b before FEC; InfiniBand coding varies by generation...'. The book is correct on the standard: IEEE 802.3bs defines the PCS for both 200GbE and 400GbE with exactly this transcode — IEEE (Gustlin) presentation: 'Both 200GBASE-R and 400GBASE-R are based on a 64B/66B code... The 64B/66B code is then transcoded to 256B/257B encoding to reduce the overhead and make room for Forward Error Correction (FEC)' (matches the book's sentence verbatim in substance); Ethernet Alliance blog: 'it was decided to reuse... the transcoding and RS‑FEC from 802.3bj for the PCS for 200 Gigabit Ethernet (200GbE) and 400 Gigabit Ethernet (400GbE)'; Wikipedia: 'The 400 Gigabit Ethernet and 200 Gigabit Ethernet standard developed by the IEEE P802.3bs Task Force'. The finding's claim (256b/257b belongs only to 400G/800G; 200GbE has no such stage) is false; its standard citations are also wrong: 802.3ck is 100G/lane (no 800G), the 400G multi-lane 256b/257b came from 802.3bs/802.3bj, and '200GbE (802.3cd)... two lanes' is wrong (802.3cd 200G = four lanes KR4/CR4).
